case_title: SUNIL MAHADEO JADHAV v. THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, who were police officials, were prosecuted for the custodial death of a person. The deceased was arrested from his house in the midnight of 16.12.1985 and lodged in police lock-up. The deceased was found dead in the lock-up of the police station in the morning of 17.12.1985. The prosecution alleged that the deceased was beaten and died as a result of injuries caused during his custody. The defense claimed that the deceased was not picked up from his house but from a Chowk and that injuries were noticed at the time of arrest. The trial court acquitted all accused, but the High Court convicted the accused under various sections of the IPC. The Supreme Court held that the accused were responsible for the injuries on the deceased's body, which led to his death, and convicted the accused under Section 304 IPC instead of 302, reducing the sentence to seven years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 3000.
